findings.description: applyHardStopMember (actors.js:1529) kills the member process (hardTerminateMemberByLauncherChildren, :1548) BEFORE writing the shutdown/termination markers (:1601-1611). Skip guard #2 relies on those markers, so a sweep landing in the kill->markers window sees pidAlive===false (state:'dead') with no markers and false-fires a member-crashed alert for an intentional /stop-member.
findings.resolution: Plan now hoists a pre-kill shutdownRequested:true intent write into applyHardStopMember before the kill (mirroring the soft path at :1451-1457), keeping the terminationKind/terminatedAt audit write after the kill. Added as in-scope + a regression test forcing a sweep in the window. (rubber-duck)

findings.description: The plan framed the explicit latch reset as optional hygiene, claiming a resumed member naturally gets a new signature. But same-session /resume-crew reuses sessionId (actors.js:687-696) and launcher.pid is rewritten only at runtime by the launcher script (actors.js:2435-2436), NOT by repairManifestForResume. A re-crash before the new launcher.pid is written would carry the OLD corpse signature and be suppressed.
findings.resolution: Added takeoverAt (stamped on every resume/takeover, actors.js:522,533) to the dead signature so resume reliably changes it; reframed the explicit reset as REQUIRED (GC + failed-spawn window). (rubber-duck)

findings.description: Stop only drains its own mailbox when listenerState !== 'armed' (hooks/stop.js:896). A normal lead between turns has an armed listener, so the plan's claim that a Stop-time sweep 'surfaces the crash in the SAME Stop turn' is false for the armed case; the appended envelope is delivered by the listener instead.
findings.resolution: Reframed D-003: armed lead -> listener delivers (= D-001 path); unarmed lead -> Stop's own consumeMailbox surfaces it same-turn. Split the D-003 AC accordingly. (copilot)

findings.description: Members can have null createdBy (assignMemberRole seeds without it, actors.js:719-728; only /spawn-member sets {leadName}, spawn-member.js:169-193). Raw createdBy.leadName misses string forms; raw readCrewMeta().leads can include tombstoned leads, so the single-lead determination is unreliable -> a crashed null-createdBy member may be claimed by no lead and never alert.
findings.resolution: Use the existing createdByLeadName() helper (stop.js:392 / actors.js:1376) + activeLeadNames() (actors.js:849) for single-lead determination; log member-crash-sweep-orphan-skipped for unclaimable null-createdBy members. (rubber-duck + copilot consensus)

findings.description: snapshotCrew() calls getMemberHealth for EVERY listNames entry (leads + tasks too). Making getMemberHealth member-role-strict or changing existing return fields would regress /crews-list-members and status surfaces.
findings.resolution: Plan now requires the getMemberHealth extension to be STRICTLY additive; health.test asserts the existing shape is unchanged. (copilot)

findings.description: If appendSystemMailbox succeeds but the subsequent latch write fails, the next sweep can re-notify the same incarnation (duplicate).
findings.resolution: Documented as intentional fail-loud/fail-duplicate: persist latch only after append; log member-crash-latch-write-failed; unit test for append-ok-but-latch-write-fail. (copilot)

findings.description: AC 'within the throttled sweep cadence' overpromises latency for the no-launcher-pid case, which deriveHealthState does not classify dead until heartbeat age >= HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS (hooks/health.js:54-57).
findings.resolution: Split ACs: pid-gone crashes wake within sweep cadence (~60s); no-pid/stale crashes within HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS (5min) + cadence. (rubber-duck + copilot consensus)
